Which ice hockey leagues and events do you cover?

We have ice hockey betting tips for the NHL, including all the major matches across the USA and Canada that build towards the Stanley Cup. You'll find NHL predictions here throughout the season, playoffs included.

We also provide ice hockey betting tips for the top leagues in Europe — including the Swedish Hockey League (SHL), the Deutsche Eishockey Liga (DEL), the Swiss National League, the Finnish Liiga and the Elite Ice Hockey League (EIHL) — as well as the Champions Hockey League and the IIHF World Championship.
When will you have ice hockey betting tips?

The National Hockey League runs from late September through to June, so during this period you'll find plenty of NHL betting tips on this page.

The British Elite League and the Swedish Hockey League both run from September to April.

Between them, these leagues mean there are ice hockey betting predictions to be found across most of the year.

We cover the regular season and the playoffs in all of the leagues mentioned, as well as outright betting tips.

When NHL Betting Peaks

Tip volume builds through the regular season and reaches its peak in the spring, when the Stanley Cup playoffs get under way. Sixteen teams — eight from each conference — compete across four best-of-seven rounds, so a single playoff run can stretch to well over twenty games.

With every series a best-of-seven and games coming thick and fast, the playoffs are the busiest time on this page for NHL predictions, right through to the Stanley Cup Final. It's also when you'll find the most outright betting tips, as tipsters weigh up who goes all the way.

This market is a simple bet on whether the designated home or away team will win. In the NHL, the money line is always two-way — overtime and a shootout are included. For European leagues, check whether your bookmaker offers a two-way (including OT) or three-way (regulation only) market, as this affects how the bet settles.

What you'll see are the odds for either team. For example, the home team may be 4/7 to win, meaning if you staked £10 and it was successful, your return would be £15.71 — a profit of £5.71.

If instead you fancy the away team, you would back them: say their money line odds were 6/4 and you staked £10, you could win as much as £25 (£15 profit) if successful.

You might want to add NHL money line picks to an accumulator. This builds up the odds for a bigger potential return, but every selection has to win for that return to pay out.

NHL Accumulator Example

As an example, imagine backing four home favourites to win on the same night:

  1. Selection 1 — 4/7 (1.57)
  2. Selection 2 — 4/6 (1.67)
  3. Selection 3 — 8/13 (1.62)
  4. Selection 4 — 2/5 (1.40)

Converting the fractions to decimal odds is the easiest way to estimate a return: multiply the odds together (1.57 × 1.67 × 1.62 × 1.40), which here gives 5.95.

That means the accumulator, if all four selections win, would return roughly £59.50 from a £10 stake — a profit of £49.50.

As well as the money line market, you'll find tips on two other markets here for today's NHL predictions. The first is spread betting, better known as the Puck Line in the NHL.

It works the same way as Asian handicap betting in football or the run line in baseball: the favourite is given a handicap to overcome, while the underdog gets a head start to defend.

In the NHL, this line is usually set at 1.5, so the favourite is given a handicap of -1.5 and the underdog gets +1.5. It can occasionally differ — 0.5 or 2.5, for instance — depending on how strong the favourite is.

To settle the bet: if the team with the -1.5 handicap wins by two or more goals, that line wins; otherwise, the +1.5 line wins.

The other market available is NHL Totals betting, where you bet on how many goals will be scored in the game.

Check your bookmaker for details, but nearly all NHL games include goals scored in overtime and penalties, while for some European leagues those may not count.

You'll get an over and an under option, the same as betting on the totals in the NBA, the runs in the MLB, or the points in the NFL.

You'll be given a line, and for NHL totals this can differ from game to game — the most common is 5.5.

That means your bet is on whether there will be under 5.5 goals (five or fewer) or over 5.5 goals (six or more).

Sometimes the line comes without a .5, such as 6.0, which brings the 'push' option into play: if the game finishes with exactly six goals, your stake is refunded.
How to follow our ice hockey tipsters

Some of our tipsters specialise in NHL betting tips, others focus on the European leagues, and some post predictions across all ice hockey.

For each tip on this page you'll see the tipster's record, so you can judge their form before following a selection. The profit figure is based on the last six months of that tipster's ice hockey picks, and looking across those months also shows how consistent they've been — a tipster who has been profitable in most of the last six months has shown steady returns.

If you want to follow particular tipsters, you can do so on the site or in the OLBG app. On the site, use the follow button on a tipster's profile or alongside their tips, and their selections will then appear in your OLBG feed. In the OLBG app, add them to MyTipsters and you'll get an alert whenever they post an ice hockey tip.

Our ice hockey tipsters add comments to their tips explaining the thinking behind each selection, so you get the reasoning as well as the pick. Reading how different tipsters view the same game — and deciding which case you find most convincing — is a good way to shape your own bets.

Whichever ice hockey tips you choose to follow, treat them as opinions to inform your own decisions, not as guarantees — no prediction is certain, and you should only ever bet what you can afford to lose. Which Hockey League Is Best for Backing Favourites?

In comparison to the other US sports, basketball is at the top of the pile for winning favourites; then it's the NFL, with baseball at the bottom of the pile.

So where does the NHL fit in? It sits about on par with baseball at the bottom, with favourites not as successful as they are in the other sports.

Below, we compare major hockey leagues from around the world and look at which have the better records for winning favourites.

Looking across the leagues for winning favourites, it is the French Ligue Magnus which comes out on top with 69.45% of favourites winning overall — a high return and over 3% clear of any other league we have looked at.

The figures favour those with home ice, with 71.55% of favourites winning at home and 65.98% on the road, which is a high number for winning favourites away from home.

The NHL comes well down the list, near the bottom for winning favourites with a 60.63% win rate, which shows just how competitive the league is.

The SHL (Swedish Hockey League) is arguably the second most popular hockey league in the world, and it sits at the foot of the table with just 58.51% of favourites winning.

It is no surprise to see those two leagues low down; both are popular because they attract many of the world's best players, which makes them competitive and means favourites can struggle.

Which Hockey Leagues Produce the Most Goals?

Now we compare the same leagues and look at which are most productive for scoring goals, over the last five completed seasons for each league.

Like the favourites, it is the French Ligue Magnus which comes out towards the top, this time for the average number of goals per game with 6.27; however, it is the UK Elite League which tops the list with an average of 6.33 goals per game.

Only four leagues surpass an average of 6 goals per game; in addition to those two, the Danish Metal Ligaen averages 6.21 and the NHL averages 6.23, with the rest all averaging under 6 goals per game.

The Czech Extraliga is the lowest-scoring of the leagues here; it averages just 5.35 goals per game, and only 40.67% of games saw six goals or more.
